title: One meal, four jobs
description: A family meal cooked by a crew runs on job titles, not on one tired person doing everything. Split any meal into four jobs — planner, shopper, cook, host — and rotate them weekly.

body.heading: The four jobs
paragraphs: The planner picks the meal and writes the list. The shopper gathers ingredients and keeps the budget. The cook runs the stove and the timings. The host sets the table, serves, and leads the clearing. Every job is real work, and every job is visible.

Rotation is the point: the person who only ever washes up never learns the timings, and the person who only ever cooks never sees the cost. A month of rotation gives everyone the full picture of what a meal actually takes.

body.heading: Start smaller than you think
paragraphs: Begin with one crew meal a week and a simple menu. Give the youngest crew member a job with real edges — washing, tearing, timing, tasting — rather than a pretend task; people rise to genuine responsibility and wilt under fake jobs.
Debrief over the meal itself: what ran late, what was wasted, what to repeat. A kitchen crew that reviews itself gets faster and calmer within a month.

takeaway: Planner, shopper, cook, host — rotate the four jobs weekly and a family meal becomes a crew performance everyone understands, instead of one person's invisible work.
